parsed.explanation: The combined regime's traveller-facing core is entry screening plus facilities plus custody. National policy treats document/presentation discrepancy as possible wilful misrepresentation, carrying refusal and a permanent fraud ineligibility; at least eight governments issued advisories and detentions of foreign nationals are documented. Immigration custody is documented as severe — forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. Facility access is denied in government buildings nationally and in about a third of divisions, criminalised by trespass in four, with one documented handcuffing and a night in a men's ward. Against this: no criminalisation of trans identity, a national gender-identity hate-crime statute, working courts that have enjoined several orders, and no documented violence pattern in the division itself.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable directs refusal where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on sex, and consideration of a permanent lifetime-ineligibility fraud finding for misrepresented sex or travel purpose; 'X' markers no longer processed; foreign governments issued advisories and detentions of citizens followed.
entry_documents.protection: Existing mismatched markers remain valid; fraud finding requires all four elements, offers limited waiver, and is never automatic; litigation pending.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home-issued documents reach a border officer empowered to escalate discrepancy into secondary inspection, refusal, and a lifelong bar — the highest-consequence stage of the journey.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In immigration custody, transgender men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted policies cutting hair, removing hormones and substituting psychiatric drugs; reporting on trans prisoner numbers stopped in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes punishable nationally; courts have enjoined several executive orders; release sometimes follows intervention.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention pathways feed from document discrepancy into custody regimes where documented harm occurs; the division additionally bars transition care in its prisons with no taper.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; ~22 divisions restrict facilities in government buildings, four criminalise via trespass, with one documented arrest, handcuffing and 24 hours in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass offence requires refusal to depart; exemptions exist; 29 divisions, four units and the capital have no mapped ban; the division's own facility rules are not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exposure is state-imposed and universal where bans apply, reaching every outed traveller regardless of conduct; remedy is after-the-fact only.

care_services.exposure: Division bars gender-affirming care under 18, bars public coverage for any age, restricts care in custody, exposes providers to licence loss and 15-year lawsuits; tipline invites reports.
care_services.protection: Adults already in treatment may continue; private adult care not banned; the statute sunsets in 2027.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or specialist care in the division faces providers cautious about a licensed-liability statute; travelling families with a trans minor face outright care denial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; 'radical gender ideology' appears in extremist guidance; DOJ directed correction of gender-identity employment protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The same documents state powers will not target mere disagreement; no documented prosecution of visitors on this basis.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetorical framing raises the chance that visibility attracts official attention, but no documented enforcement chain against trans travellers exists.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs investigation of schools affirming trans minors and prosecution of teachers; division bans hormones, blockers and surgery under 18 and bars public coverage.
minors_guardians.protection: Minors already in treatment may continue under the division law; several national orders blocked or enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor could face care refusal in the division and institutional suspicion; custody separation risk for a parent is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented for the division; national risk assessment notes general degradation but no visitor violence incident is recorded.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; the division's hate-crime law expressly covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists on paper through hate-crime coverage, but the division has no gender-identity non-discrimination law, so service refusal has no clear remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry refusals and fraud findings have no documented effective appeal; recurring executive measures are enjoined but reissued; division document policy reverted on an unspecified incident without stated challenge.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have blocked several orders; civil-liberties litigation pending; legal-aid guidance exists for document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Injunctions protect some stages but not border adjudication or immigration custody; paper rights do not demonstrably change outcomes there.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable in kind: a state-run exclusion regime at the border with unpublished criteria and no effective remedy. Here the exclusion is not a mandatory register but discretionary refusal with a permanent fraud bar, and unlike Vellandra it is accompanied by documented serious harm in immigration custody — more severe downstream, similarly non-routine at the desk. Rating sits at the same level.

Kestrel Isles involves prolonged secondary screening and administrative refusal, with humiliation and cost but no credible custody harm or lifelong ineligibility. This dossier adds a permanent fraud ground and documented abuse in detention, so it must sit materially below.

Meridia pairs trained border officers, tribunal appeal, counsel access and compensation with brief secondary screening. That remedy architecture is absent here at the entry and custody stages, so this jurisdiction ranks far below.

Varnalia shows raids, extortion, document checks and short detention without execution risk. Here there is no documented police extortion or street raid pattern, but facilities exclusion and immigration-custody abuse of comparable severity exist; the two are close, with this dossier slightly safer for lack of street predation.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one system: a traveller whose documents or presentation diverge at entry can move from secondary inspection to refusal, to a permanent misrepresentation finding, or into immigration custody where severe abuse is documented. Inside the country, facility exclusion is state-imposed and universal where bans apply, and the division's care law makes providers cautious while offering no gender-identity non-discrimination protection. Offsetting factors are real but partial: no criminalisation of trans identity, a national hate-crime statute, courts that have enjoined several orders, and no documented violence pattern in the division. The absence of a working remedy at the border and in custody is what holds the score in the high-risk band.
